learning: Track width has moved the score monotonically from 0.10 to 0.14 m. The 0.16 m race tests whether the trend continues or the slalom's tight bends start to lose line. Read s-bend finishes, max_error peaks and slalom line_loss_events per track.
notes: Single-variable test: wheel_track 0.14 to 0.16 m, with the iteration 4 controller unchanged. Expected to continue the monotonic track trend if the s-bend and oval hold up.
rationale: Evidence: iteration 4 (wheel_track 0.14 m, all other fields as iteration 1) is the best design at 517.07. Across clean wheel-track points, score rises monotonically with width: 0.10 m gave 357.3 (iteration 3), 0.12 m gave 482.7 (iteration 1), 0.14 m gave 517.1 (iteration 4). Oval finishes are 20/20 at 0.14 m, and s-bend finishes rose to 6/20 with mean score 519. Slalom is still 0/20 with about 0.9 line-loss events per run. Every failure is an off-track end with max_error at or above 0.06 m, while rms_error stays at 0.026 to 0.031 m, so the limit is occasional bend excursions. Decision: keep the iteration 4 geometry and controller and change only wheel_track from 0.14 to 0.16 m, as the Builder proposed. Turn rate per PWM unit scales as 1/wheel_track, so yaw authority falls by about 0.875x. I do not rescale kp: iterations 2 and 3 lowered kp for narrower tracks and lost score, and keeping kp at 1.6 keeps this a single-variable test. Expected result (hypothesis, not measured): s-bend finishes at or above 6/20, score at or above 517, and the slalom's line-loss events may rise because turn authority is lower there. Controller stays as iteration 4: base_speed 1.0, kp 1.6, ki 0.05, kd 0.5, weights -1.5 to +1.5 on the seven sensors, and last_direction line-loss recovery.
